newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt detains nine Shi'ites for sedition.
newsitem.headline: Egypt detains nine Shi'ites for sedition.

text.p: Egyptian authorities have detained nine Shi'ite Moslems on suspicion of belonging to an illegal organisation trying to transform Egypt into a strict Islamist state similiar to Iran, official sources said on Tuesday.

They said police arrested the nine men in Cairo last week. Police also seized large amounts of printed and recorded speeches of Iranian clerics and plans to infiltrate Egyptian political parties and use them to gain power.
The sources said the state prosecutor ordered the nine held in custody for 15 days pending investigations. They said the men had escaped a widescale crackdown on Shi'ites last year.
Egypt arrested 56 men in October on suspicion of trying to recruit followers to promote Shi'ite ideas.
Shi'ism, the sect of Islam dominant in Iran, is not illegal in overwhelmingly Sunni Egypt but the government is wary of any Iranian religious influence.

The government newspaper al-Akhbar said the nine men would probably face charges of "belonging to an illegal group with aims including subverting the constitution, preventing authorities from enforcing it, harming national unity and social order, and exploiting religion by spoken and written propaganda of fundamentalist ideas and seditious influence".

Cairo has often accused Tehran of trying to export its brand of Islam and says Iran has financed and supported the Islamist militants fighting the police in the south of Egypt. Iran denies the accusations and says Cairo blames it to cover up internal problems rooted in Egypt's pro-Western policies.
About 1,000 people have been killed in the conflict between Moslem militants and the Egyptian state since 1992.

The Shi'ites differ with the Sunnis originally over who should have led the Moslem community on the death of the Prophet Mohammad. Many differences over doctrine, religious law and political organisation have since developed.
